facts.statement: The genus name Osteolepis was first coined in 1829 by Sedgwick and Murchison.
facts.quote: The name Osteolepis was first used in 1829 by authors Sedgwick and Murchison

facts.statement: A detailed scientific description of the genus was published in 1835 by the naturalist Louis Agassiz.
facts.quote: a detailed description of the genus was not published until 1835 when naturalist Louis Agassiz treated the genus in more detail

facts.statement: The species O. panderi was named in 1948 by the paleontologist Erik Jarvik.
facts.quote: In 1948 paleontologist Erik Jarvik named this species O. panderi

facts.statement: Osteolepis is an extinct genus of lobe-finned fish that lived during the Devonian period.
facts.quote: Osteolepis (from 'bone' and 'scale') is an extinct genus of lobe-finned fish from the Devonian period

facts.statement: Osteolepis lived in Lake Orcadie in northern Scotland.
facts.quote: It lived in Lake Orcadie of northern Scotland

facts.statement: Osteolepis was approximately 20 centimeters long and covered in large, square scales.
facts.quote: Osteolepis was about 20 cm long, and covered with large, square scales

facts.statement: The scales and head plates of Osteolepis were covered by a thin layer of spongy bone called cosmine.
facts.quote: The scales and plates on its head were covered in a thin layer of spongy, bony material called cosmine

facts.statement: Canals connecting the cosmine layer to sensory cells likely allowed Osteolepis to sense vibrations in the water.
facts.quote: These canals ended in pores on the surface and were probably for sensing vibrations in the water

facts.statement: Osteolepis likely fed on small invertebrates like arthropods and mollusks.
facts.quote: Osteolepis likely fed on small invertebrates such as arthropods and mollusks

facts.statement: Osteolepis was likely prey for larger fish such as Cheirolepis.
facts.quote: and itself may have been prey for larger fish such as Cheirolepis

facts.statement: Osteolepis lived in the Orcadian lakes of northern Scotland.
facts.quote: Vivieron en los lagos Orcadianos del norte de Escocia

facts.statement: Osteolepis was a rhipidistian fish that shared several characteristics with tetrapods.
facts.quote: Osteolepis era un ripidistiano, que tenía varias características en común con los tetrápodos

facts.statement: Osteolepis was a tetrapodomorph distantly related to tetrapods.
facts.quote: Osteolepis was a tetrapodomorph, and was distantly related to tetrapods

facts.statement: Osteolepis belongs to the family Osteolepididae and the order Osteolepiformes.
Osteolepis lived from the Eifelian to the Famennian stages, between 393.47 and 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Eifelian to Famennian (393.47 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: The habitat of Osteolepis was a calm freshwater lake that experienced periodic drying.
facts.quote: This environment was a calm freshwater lake, and was subject to periodic desiccation

facts.statement: Anoxic events in deep water likely caused mass fish kills that preserved articulated fossils of Osteolepis.
facts.quote: During periods where the water was deepest, anoxic (without oxygen) events would result in fish kills, creating the large assemblages of articulated fish fossils that include Osteolepis

facts.statement: Species O. arenatus, O. microlepidotus, and O. major are now considered synonymous with the type species O. macrolepidotus.
facts.quote: The species O. arenatus and O. microlepidotus, as well as the species O. major which Agassiz named in 1845, have since been considered identical to the type species O. macrolepidotus

facts.statement: It is debated whether early distinctions between Osteolepis species were based on real anatomy or taphonomic artifacts.
facts.quote: The features used to distinguish these species were largely the result of taphonomy, rather than actual anatomical distinctions
